title: Memory Keeper: AI for Organizational Decision Traceability
abstract: Critical business decisions do not happen in isolation in a particular location; rather, the operational environment in which such business decisions take place gets dispersed in messaging conversations, email threads, and meeting discussions. It may not be feasible to follow the rationale for a particular business decision taken months ago. In the end, the process becomes obscure, and there is a marked lack of traceability. A hybrid solution named Memory Keeper is proposed to overcome the problem of data silos. By combining Knowledge Graphs (KG) with vector stores to build an improved Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) model, the framework continuously feeds distributed communication flows into the model. It processes unstructured information to identify essential decisions and maps structural relationships between stakeholders, timelines, and topics into a queryable KG. Although conventional semantic search approaches usually ignore the interdependencies of events, Memory Keeper can retrieve historical context with high accuracy by using graph-based reasoning to route vector embeddings. This approach makes it possible to generate traceable and explainable responses to user queries, thus making enterprise knowledge an active tool that supports rapid decision-making with well-documented evidence.

Although conventional semantic search approaches usually ignore the interdependencies of events, Memory Keeper can retrieve historical context with high accuracy by using graph-based reasoning to route vector embeddings. This approach makes it possible to generate traceable and explainable responses to user queries, thus making enterprise knowledge an active tool that supports rapid decision-making with well-documented evidence.

title: GenAI in Tourism Study 2026 - LNU - Group 05
abstract: The contents of this report investigates Generative AI (GenAI) and how consumers experience and use it within tourism. The purpose is to understand how GenAI tools influenced the interviewees' experiences, both from a past and future perspective. Therefore, the research question is: How does GenAI influence the experiences within tourism in the context of the past and future? To answer this question, a qualitative method was applied through the use of semi-structured interviews. From these answers, three main dimensions were formed. Firstly, GenAI as a Practical and Cognitive Support of Tourism, which was found to help manage information for the interviewees as well as plan, personalise and make decisions for their travels. This helped alleviate mental stresses they may have faced. The second dimension was GenAI as an Influence for Social Interactions and Experiences in Tourism, which highlighted how people have changed how they interact with staff, which brought concerns with some interviewees on how they have worries regarding the loss of authentic human contact when travelling. Finally, the last dimension was GenAI and its Risks, Vulnerabilities and Future Concerns, showcasing other concerns that come with AI, which include privacy and overreliance. The findings therefore showed that GenAI can enhance confidence, efficiency as well as be a convenient help within a tourism context. Although the majority of the interviewees remain cautious of the tool, they value it as a helpful addition to their travel experience instead of a replacement for human interactions. All in all, this highlights the importance of having a balance between technology and authenticity in travel.

title: paver205-png/UPAS-V-5.5-Universal-Project-Analysis-System: UPAS v5.5 — Stable Release
abstract: First public release of UPAS — Universal Project Analysis System. UPAS is a structured analytical protocol designed to run on large language models. It reflects the structure of any project back to its author through four axes of reality: physical feasibility, causal logic, agent behavior, and temporal stability. Key features in v5.5: Three independent LLM instances running in parallel Nine-block analysis covering goal audit, ethics, logic, simulation, incentives, resources, and failure modes Stability Index with Critical Flags and Confidence Coefficient Principle of Structural Compression at the formalization stage Divergence reporting as a structural signal, not a system error The protocol is the product. Open for use, adaptation, and improvement.
